Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City htt : //www.dilg.com. h DILG OPINION No. Yo s. 2323 APR 27 2023 Ms. LORRAIN GAY F. BILOG bilog.lorrain_gay@dpwh.ph Dear Ms. Bilog: This refers to your letter dated December 7, 2022 requesting this Department's legal opinion relative to interpretation/application of Executive Order No. 02, Series of 2022 (An Executive Order Setting the Guidelines for the Implementation of Alert 2 of Covid- 19 Response in the City of General Santo and other Purposes", issued by Office of the City Mayor, General Santos City. Per your letter, hereunder are the pertinent factual antecedents: On September 28, 2022, you were scheduled to take a trip to General Santos City for work purposes, and you intended to take your son with you. Unfortunately, your son was not able to join you because Philippine Airlines (PAL) requires a negative RT-PCR result pursuant to Executive Order No. 2, series of 2022. You negotiated with PAL supervisors to let your son do an anti-gen test so you both could board the plane together as scheduled, but to no avail. Instead, PAL insisted that they stick to the aforesaid Executive Order. Apparently, prior to your scheduled trip, you have checked for the alert level status of General Santos City and per Department of Health General Santos City was already in alert level I. Upon arrival in General you have inquired and was told by the City Health Office (CHO) that "[General Santos City] is already in Alert Level 1, so there are no travel restrictions anymore based on IATF Guidelines". Premised from the foregoing, arose your query. At the outset, it is important to note that the issuance of the subject Executive Order in question does not carry with it a permanent application and effect, being subject to subsequent issuances according to the prevailing situation in light of the COVID-19 pandemic. Stated differently, it was issued in an interim manner. Section 1 thereof explicitly provides that "[T"he guidelines set [forth] herein shall cover the periods from February 16 to 28, 2022, or during such periods when the city is placed under Alert Level 2 by the national IA TF. " Accordingly, the guidelines under such an executive order are therefore assumed to be lifted after the date specified therein, at which point they will no longer have any bearing. Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Premised from the foregoing, it is this Department's view that the invocation of the subject Executive Order by PAL—the reason why your son was prevented from boarding the plane as scheduled—is clearly improper. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, B e Authority of the Secretary: T . JUA VICTOR R.
